text:
alex: quick sync — proposal: introduce a lightweight ingest gate that runs a micro-benchmark + compatibility quickchecks before queuing a model for the full bench pipeline. goal: catch obvious failures early and avoid spending full-bench cycles on obviously incompatible models.

maria: sounds good. main worry is false negatives that block fine models. what's the failure/override UX?

jamal: can we make it tenant-aware? allow opt-out for enterprise customers or a per-customer whitelist. also we'll want a plugin API for custom validators.

lina: idea: preflight = fingerprint + shape/op-set check + perf_smoke (512 tokens x 3 seeds). if preflight passes -> enqueue full bench. if fails -> fast feedback with logs and repro. cheap but actionable.

diego: how do we surface results? console needs pass/fail, failure_reason, short logs, and a link to the full artifact. reuse existing admit API?

alex: prefer a loosely-coupled approach: admit-service emits a preflight report (signed artifact in storage) and a small JSON summary. bench orchestrator consumes the artifact. keeps bench-runner decoupled.

maria: also include runtime ABI + quantization profile in the report so we don't get runtime surprises when serving.

jamal: tradeoff: more checks = more latency on initial ingest. maybe run preflight async but allow immediate test-only access (internal tokens) so product teams can iterate.

lina: UX suggestion: model state 'ingest-pending' -> limited internal allowlist -> show preflight status in model detail. slack notif on fail/pass.

diego: example preflight config snippet: 
```
preflight:
  tests:
    - fingerprint
    - shape_check
    - perf_smoke
  perf_smoke:
    tokens: 512
    seeds: 3
```

alex: ops question — where run perf_smoke? cheap CPU quantized path won't catch kv-cache perf. leaning towards small GPU pool (short lived instances) to capture real latency/kv behavior. thoughts?

maria: small GPU pool makes sense. we should record token-level latency distribution and mem_peak. those are critical for admission decisions.

jamal: metrics to emit: preflight.pass (bool), pass_rate, median_latency_512, p95_latency_512, mem_peak_bytes, mismatch_hash_count. these let us tune thresholds.

lina: rollout policy: pass -> enqueue bench; fail -> auto-open ticket with attachments (preflight logs + repro script). include a "compatibility_hint" field for remediation suggestions.

diego: example hint: "unsupported_op: aten::quantize_per_tensor" or "missing_kv_cache_handling" — could be generated by validator plugins.

admit-bot: created preflight artifact s3://redwood-preflight/2287650000/summary.json (signed).

alex: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with API protobufs for the preflight report schema and the minimal JSON summary. ping me if you want co-author.

maria: I'll add a privacy/contract note: customer models must have their preflight artifacts stored under customer-controlled buckets or access-restricted storage and audit logs enabled.

jamal: acceptance criteria idea: (1) teams can opt models in/out per-customer, (2) preflight summary appears in Console within 10m of ingest, (3) bench cost savings: at least 50% reduction in full-bench cycles wasted on obviously incompatible models within first 3 months.

lina: technical acceptance: preflight should complete <10m for 95% of cases; perf_smoke uses <=3 runs; artifacts include reproducible minimal repro.

alex: great. I'll post RFC in #eng-ml tomorrow morning with a proto sketch and proposed thresholds. :thumbsup:
